## The equation-of-state and positivity status of a block (`EfStatus`) {#sec-ch08-efstatus}

### Summary

Every mechanism of this chapter leaves a trace: a floor that patched a cell, a NaN that was zeroed, a vapour column
that could not be repaired, a limiter factor below one. This section is where those traces are kept. Each block owns
one `EfStatus`, a fixed set of named device tensors, its slots. The equation of state, the tracer and scalar
limiters and the fourth-order conversion write into the slots in place, during the stages, without reading anything
back to the host. Two readers use them after the stages: the redo decision of @sec-ch08-redo reads the marks and the
failure counts in its one device-to-host copy, and the budget's cycle line reads the positivity meters. A captured
stage (@sec-ch11) runs its segments several times before it records them, so the executor saves every slot before
those warm-up runs and restores it afterwards; a warm-up therefore leaves no count.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One record per block of what the floors, repairs and limiters did in the step; @tbl-ch08-efstatus-slots.

**Data.** Ten slots, each a device tensor (bool, int32, int64 or FP64), on the block's device.

**Placement.** Written in the stages; marks and flags reset at stage 0; read by `check_redo` and the cycle line.

**Activation.** Always present; a slot exists once its writer has run or its module has bound it.

**Guarantee / limits.** A record, not a repair. The meters are not rolled back by a redo (Limits).

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch08-efstatus-tests.
:::

Local symbols: none. The section names slots by their code names (`kMarks`, `kPosHits`, ...).

### Derivation

There is no equation to derive: `EfStatus` is a record. What has to be shown is that the record means the same
thing however the stage runs. Three properties of the code give that.

1. **No host read inside a stage.** Every writer updates its slot with a tensor operation on the device: `mark` ORs
   a 0-d boolean into an entry ({{< code src/eos/ef_status.hpp EfStatus >}}), the census adds a sum
   ({{< code src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp PositivityLimiter::census_ >}}), the vapour repair adds its failure count
   on the device on CUDA ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}).
   So a stage that writes the record can be captured as a CUDA graph.
2. **One owner of each tensor.** A meter slot is the same tensor its module registers as a buffer: `bind` stores
   the tensor in the slot and returns it for `register_buffer` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}};
   {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::reset >}}). The buffer names (`positivity_hits`, `lim_cut`, ...) and
   the slot are two names of one tensor, so moving the module to another device moves the slot with it.
3. **Warm-ups leave no count.** The executor's save list holds every defined slot, under the key `efs.<n>`
   ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::save_list >}}). Before a capture's three eager warm-up runs the
   listed tensors are cloned, and afterwards the clones are copied back into them, so a count a warm-up added is removed before the
   recorded run. Without this, a capture would count its segment four times (three warm-ups and the recorded run),
   which is what the graph test of @tbl-ch08-efstatus-tests was written to catch.

### Numerical method

The slots, their types and their writers and readers at the pin are in @tbl-ch08-efstatus-slots. The order of the
enumeration is the order of the record; `kNumSlots` is its length.

| slot | type | written by | reset | read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kMarks` | bool $[2]$: [0] a floor patched an interior cell, [1] an interior NaN | the conserved and primitive limiter passes (@sec-ch08-eoslimiter) | stage 0 and after a redo decision (`reset_limiter_marks`) | the redo decision, as the limiter and NaN causes |
| `kVaporFail` | int32, 0-d | the vapour column repair inside a stage or `check_redo` (@sec-ch08-fixvapor) | stage 0; after `check_redo` reads it | the redo decision, folded into the limiter cause |
| `kHeatCapacity` | bool, 0-d | the ideal-moist heat-capacity check | stage 0 (`clear_heat_capacity_failure`) | the redo decision, folded into the limiter cause |
| `kPosHits` | int64 $[1]$ | the tracer limiter's census (@sec-ch08-theta) | never (run-to-date) | the `positivity_hits` buffer |
| `kPosSevere` | int64 $[1]$ | the same | never | the cycle line, `thetasevere` |
| `kPosMin` | FP64 $[1]$ (wide dtype) | the same, as a running minimum | never (starts at 1) | the cycle line, `thetamin` |
| `kLimCut` | FP64 $[1]$ (wide dtype) | the tracer limiter, $x_1$ faces: the flux removed | never | the cycle line, `limcut` as `kLimCut`/`kLimFlux` |
| `kLimFlux` | FP64 $[1]$ (wide dtype) | the same: the flux offered | never | the same |
| `kScalarPosHits` | int64 $[1]$ | the passive-scalar limiters (@sec-ch08-scalar) | never | the scalar's `positivity_hits` buffer |
| `kConvTrips` | int64 $[1]$, defined at conversion order 4 only | the fourth-order conversion, cells that kept the second-order primitives (@sec-ch04) | never | the `conversion_trips` buffer |

: The slots of `EfStatus` at the pin ({{< code src/eos/ef_status.hpp EfStatus >}}). "Wide dtype" is the precision
policy's wide type, FP64 except on MPS (@sec-ch12). {#tbl-ch08-efstatus-slots}

The marks and the two failure flags describe one step: stage 0 resets them in `stage_advance`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}), and `local_redo_flag_tensor`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}) stacks them with the floor test,
the implicit clamp and the saturation and solve failures into the flag vector of @sec-ch08-redo. The meters describe
the run: they are created at zero (`kPosMin` at one) when the hydro module is reset
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}) and only added to afterwards. `print_cycle_line`
({{< code src/diagnostics/budget.cpp print_cycle_line >}}) reads `kLimCut`, `kLimFlux` and `kPosSevere` of every local
block to the host, sums them over blocks and ranks, takes the minimum of `kPosMin`, and prints them under
"run-to-date" as `limcut=` (removed over offered), `thetamin=` and `thetasevere=`; `limcut` is printed only when
some flux was offered.

No figure: the record has no geometry, and @tbl-ch08-efstatus-slots is its whole content.

: Code map of the block status record. {#tbl-ch08-efstatus-code}

An equation of state that is not attached to a block keeps a record of its own, so a direct call (a test, a Python
conversion) still has somewhere to write (`own_status_`,
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::ef_status >}}). Nothing reads that private record in a
run.

**How to use it.** Nothing is configured. From Python the meters are the hydro module's buffers
`positivity_hits`, `positivity_severe`, `positivity_min`, `lim_cut`, `lim_flux` and, at conversion order 4,
`conversion_trips`, and the scalar module's `positivity_hits`. The cycle line prints the run-to-date summary
whenever the driver calls `print_cycle_info` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_output.cpp MeshBlockImpl::print_cycle_info >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_cycle_diagnostics.cpp` (`test_cycle_diagnostics.release`), case `cycle_info.positivity_meters_read_their_hand_computed_values` | a six-cell column whose cloud settles at $-2$ m s$^{-1}$ for one step of 1 s: $\Theta = 0.5$ in the five draining cells, so `positivity_min` $= 0.5$, `positivity_severe` $= 5$, `lim_flux` $= 5\cdot 2\,\rho_{\mathrm c}$ and `lim_cut`/`lim_flux` $= 0.5$; the cycle line prints `limcut=0.5`, `thetamin=0.5`, `thetasevere=5` | $10^{-9}$ (relative for the fluxes) on the buffers; $10^{-5}$ on the printed tokens | the hand computation is exact; $10^{-9}$ covers the Riemann flux of the column, about $10^{-15}$ of the settling flux, and $10^{-5}$ the printed precision ({{< code tests/test_cycle_diagnostics.cpp cycle_info.positivity_meters_read_their_hand_computed_values >}}) |
| `tests/test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager.py` (`test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager_python`) | a cuda-graph block and an eager block step the same schedule; after every step every meter, the redo result, the state and the cycle line are equal, in FP64 and FP32, for the moist case and the conversion-order-4 case; the eager meters are nonzero (the case is not vacuous) | bitwise (`torch.equal`; the cycle lines compared as strings) | graph and eager must be the same arithmetic ({{< code tests/test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager.py assert_meters >}}) |
| `tests/test_fp32_compute.py` (`test_fp32_compute_python`) | in an FP32 block, `positivity_min`, `lim_cut` and `lim_flux` are among the small diagnostics allowed to stay FP64 | exact (a dtype) | the precision policy's wide dtype |

: Tests of the block status record. {#tbl-ch08-efstatus-tests}

The meter test runs its CUDA arm only on a CUDA build; on a CPU build it checks that the cuda-graph setting runs
eager (no capture, no replay) and that its meters equal eager's, and then skips the graph part. The record of this
report was made on a CPU build, so the graph = eager claim for the meters rests on the test's CUDA arm, which this
record did not run.[^ch08-efstatus-run]

[^ch08-efstatus-run]: [sha: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062; deck: the tests' own cards; run: see the
    run record of @sec-ch08-theta, which lists the command, the build and the versions for every ctest of this chapter.]

### Limits

1. **The meters count rejected attempts.** A redo rolls back the flux register and its monitor and restores the
   state ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_redo.cpp MeshBlockImpl::apply_redo >}}), but nothing restores the
   `EfStatus` meters, so `positivity_hits`, `positivity_severe`, `positivity_min`, `lim_cut` and `lim_flux` include
   the census of attempts that were then redone. This is read from the code at the pin; no test asserts it either way.
2. **`kPosSevere` is a count of entries, not of cells.** A cell with two species below the threshold counts twice.
3. **The scalar census counts hits only.** There is no severe count, minimum or cut meter for the passive scalars.
4. **The graph = eager equality of the meters is tested on CUDA only.** On MPS the wide dtype is FP32, and no test
   of the meters runs on MPS.
